steps.speaker: Mess
steps.content: You're here!
The moment you enter the interrogation room, Mess comes up to you, excitement writ large on her face.

steps.speaker: Mess
steps.content: I'm bored to death here. When can I leave?

steps.speaker: Mess
steps.content: I've got a bunch of commissions on my hands. Can I go now? I'll come back after I finish them.
Be serious, Mess.
I know what you did; I know the game you're playing.
Now, I ask questions, you answer them. Let's get this over with.

steps.speaker: Mess
steps.content: Hehe, interesting... Are you this serious when you are interrogating other people?

steps.speaker: Mess
steps.content: All right, all right, I'll be the bigger person. Ask away!

steps.speaker: Eastside Public Security Officer
steps.content: ...The attackers are using a bomb that releases an unknown gas when detonated. If ordinary people inhale the gas, their M-values will soar, and they will become overly excited, short-tempered, and even deranged.

steps.speaker: Eastside Public Security Officer
steps.content: Some victims will assault other people indiscriminately. So far, more than 100 victims have been identified...

steps.speaker: Eastside Public Security Officer
steps.content: We haven't been able to attain a sample of the poisonous gas. When the bombs explode, the gaseous residues will dissipate completely, even if they've been kept in an airtight container, and reasons for this are unknown.

steps.speaker: Eastside Public Security Officer
steps.content: The attackers are very cautious. They seem to know their way around the network of monitoring systems in Eastside. We are unable to tracking them down.
So you haven't found any useful clues at all?

steps.speaker: Eastside Public Security Officer
steps.content: ...Not entirely. We found this.
test
test
test
test
test
test

steps.speaker: Mess
steps.content: Are you saying...

steps.speaker: Mess
steps.content: Those worthless sheriffs think I did that, because of this empty canister with the logo of my workshop on it?
You're a suspect.

steps.speaker: Mess
steps.content: But I've been here with you this whole time.

steps.speaker: Mess
steps.content: If I was out there placing gas bombs, doesn't that mean you were in on it too?

options: You might be part of a team.

choices.text: You might be part of a team.

steps.content: The weapon maker doesn't need to be present. You could totally be part of a team.

steps.speaker: Mess
steps.content: Oh, well done, Sherlock.
Mess' face takes on an expression of mock admiration.

steps.speaker: Mess
steps.content: Then what? Do you have evidence?

Unfortunately, you don't. Clues provided by the public security agency in Eastside are scarce, and the investigation conducted by the MBCC itself has failed to find anything that suggests Mess is in cahoots with someone.

steps.speaker: Mess
steps.content: No? Okay then... I've had enough of this. You have to let me go now.
Apparently, Mess had no intention of cooperating in the first place.
But you don't have the time to play charades with her now.
Listen, Mess... We haven't found out who the attackers are, and the lives of millions of Eastsiders are on the line.
I know you don't care about any of this. I know you don't care who might get hurt or die.
But I have to do my job. You'd better cooperate, or...
I'll have to be tougher with you, if push comes to shove.

steps.speaker: Mess
steps.content: Uh-huh?
Mess smiles, not intimidated by your seriousness.
It's an irritating smile.

steps.speaker: Mess
steps.content: Sigh... what choice do I have? I'm just a Sinner under detention. You have the shackles. You think I dare to disobey you?

steps.speaker: Mess
steps.content: But allow me to ask you a few questions before I answer any of yours.

steps.speaker: Mess
steps.content: Great, I knew you'd be generous. Here are my questions.
What would you do if I said no?

steps.speaker: Mess
steps.content: I'd fight you as best I can, for as long as I can.

steps.speaker: Mess
steps.content: I know that I'd eventually succumb to the invincible shackles, but still, I'd go all out to make your life miserable, even for a short time.

steps.speaker: Mess
steps.content: How's that for a plan of action?
That's not a pleasant scenario.
You don't want to waste your time engaging in a tug-of-war with her. You decide to answer her questions ASAP.
Ask your questions then.
A self-satisfied smirk curves up the corners of her mouth.

steps.speaker: Mess
steps.content: Great, here's the first one...

steps.speaker: Mess
steps.content: Is there someone in Eastside that you care about a lot?
The question catches you unawares.

steps.speaker: Mess
steps.content: No one, I suppose? I hear the new Chief of the MBCC is a poor soul who suffers from amnesia and has been made to step into the predecessor's shoes.

steps.speaker: Mess
steps.content: You've been busy putting out fires all over the place ever since you took office. Surely you haven't got around to making friends in Eastside?

steps.speaker: Mess
steps.content: Okay, you answered the first question, sort of. Here is my second question...

steps.speaker: Mess
steps.content: Are you supposed to be the one responsible for handling this gas bomb thing?

steps.speaker: Mess
steps.content: The answer is no, right? Your responsibility is limited to the capture of Sinners, and the handling of Black Rings. It shouldn't fall to you to take care of such a minor business.

steps.speaker: Mess
steps.content: Sorry, I forgot the first few questions already. Can I just answer the last one? About my works...

steps.speaker: Mess
steps.content: Have you ever asked yourself what's the point of all this?
Mess puts her hand on her mouth, as if to hide a smile.

steps.speaker: Mess
steps.content: You poor thing, being bossed around by this organization, running errands for that supervisor, day in, day out. You give it your all, you risk your life, but you don't even get a thank-you.

steps.speaker: Mess
steps.content: Think about it... Have they ever shown you one tiny bit of respect?

steps.speaker: Mess
steps.content: In their eyes, you're just a convenient tool, designed to do their dirty, taxing, and shady jobs.

steps.speaker: Mess
steps.content: If you really think about it, you're no different from those little darlings I made. Wait, no. The darlings I made are treasured and maintained well by their owners. Hahaha!

steps.speaker: Mess
steps.content: Or...
Mess leans in closer.

steps.speaker: Mess
steps.content: Maybe... you can show them that you're not a tool.

steps.speaker: Mess
steps.content: Cut open the puppeteers' hands, let them see blood... Don't you find this prospect exciting?
Mess whispers in your ear, like a demon at work.

steps.speaker: Mess
steps.content: Those arrogant high-ups must pay. ${PlayerName}, you're powerful, and you have Sinners that are truly loyal to you. That's reason enough...

steps.speaker: Mess
steps.content: Go make it happen. Stop being a puppet. And damn those idle good-for-nothings. You should be the master of the DisCity.
You're right, I should be the master of the DisCity...
When that day comes, I'll eliminate Mania and bring true peace to the city.
Mess is dumbfounded for a few moments, staring at the amusing look on your face, and then bursts into laughter.
No, I don't need that.
I only hope that Mania can be eliminated, and true peace can come to the city.
Mess is dumbfounded for a few moments, staring at your face, and then bursts into laughter.

steps.speaker: Mess
steps.content: Hahaha... Interesting, interesting indeed!

steps.speaker: Mess
steps.content: You dismissed my suggestion like it's the craziest idea in the world, even though all I did was give voice to what you desire... This is a first for me. Hahaha!

steps.speaker: Mess
steps.content: Hahaha! You're surrounded by su-ch a powerful force of dark malice, and you're not controlled by it. Are you really a human being? Hahaha...

options: Are you done with your questions?

choices.text: Are you done with your questions?

steps.speaker: Mess
steps.content: Oh, sorry, sorry... I'm done.

steps.speaker: Mess
steps.content: You don't have to say anything more. I've got the answers I need.

steps.speaker: Mess
steps.content: Quid pro quo. Now it's my turn to answer questions.
Mess sits up straighter, wipes away the tears brought forth by the bout of laughing and gives you that sly grin of hers, a grin that kind of gets on your nerves.
Before you can say anything, she picks up the small empty canister.

steps.speaker: Mess
steps.content: I know what you want to ask. Let me be straight with you... I made this.

steps.speaker: Mess
steps.content: But I'm no partner of the attackers. Or at least I don't think the customer who commissioned me to make this thing told me what it'd be used for.

steps.speaker: Mess
steps.content: As for information about this customer, I don't remember any... Sorry.
It was made no more than half a year ago. You don't remember anything about the customer?

steps.speaker: Mess
steps.content: Do you remember who you had a meal with half a year ago?

steps.speaker: Mess
steps.content: Come on, I got half a dozen commissions every week. I can't remember every little detail, can I?
Are you saying that you know nothing about this deal?

steps.speaker: Mess
steps.content: Be patient... I'm gonna help you out.

steps.speaker: Mess
steps.content: I'm still waiting for you to awe me in some way, after all...
Then what other information can you give me?

steps.speaker: Mess
steps.content: 15th Floor, 109 Garden Avenue, Eastside. The address of my private workshop.

steps.speaker: Mess
steps.content: I keep my ledger there. Every commission I have taken on in the past two years is recorded in it. With this ledger...
Mess has barely finished speaking when you stand up and turn on your communications device.
Right, get a car ready, I'm going to Eastside.

steps.speaker: Mess
steps.content: Wait, wait, I'm coming with you.
You turn around.
You're still a suspect.

steps.speaker: Mess
steps.content: I hid the ledger! And the information in it is encrypted. Only I can decipher it.

steps.speaker: Mess
steps.content: Don't look at me like that. I always take customer privacy seriously.
Looking at your cold eyes, Mess decides to play the role of a pestering child.

steps.speaker: Mess
steps.content: Could you please, please take me along? There's no harm in that. I haven't been home for a long time. I really miss it. Please, please...

steps.speaker: Mess
steps.content: You don't want to waste time decoding the information, right? You have the shackles, so you don't have to worry about losing control over me.
Right at this moment, your communications device beeps. You've heard back from your team.
You searched it? No ledger?

steps.speaker: Mess
steps.content: Well, well, well. Breaking into the room of a maiden... Is this how your MBCC does things?!
You take a look at the noisy maiden before you and decide to give in to her request.
...Yes, I'm taking Mess with me. She'll help us find and decode the ledger.

steps.speaker: Mess
steps.content: Hooray! I'm gonna buy up all the new arrivals in the shop downstairs!

steps.speaker: Mess
steps.content: Er... I use the MBCC's car to bring them back, right?
